memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: '"The Lord turn his face toward you and give you peace."' - Num 6:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The blessing reaches its climax with the greatest gift of all: peace. "The Lord turn his face toward you and give you peace." When God turns His attention fully toward us in favour, the result is peace — a deep, settled well-being that the world cannot give or take away.

The Hebrew word for peace here is "shalom." It means far more than the absence of trouble. It means wholeness, completeness, flourishing, everything being as it should be. It is life made whole under the smile of God.

This is what every human heart longs for. We chase peace in so many places — in success, in security, in relationships, in comfort. But real, lasting peace is a gift that comes from God turning His face toward us. It flows from being right with Him.

This is precisely what Jesus came to give. He is called the Prince of Peace, and through His cross He made peace between us and God (Rom 5:1; Col 1:20). Before He left His disciples, He said, "Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you... Do not let your hearts be troubled" (John 14:27).

The peace God offers is not dependent on your circumstances being easy. It is the peace of knowing that the God whose face shines upon you is for you, holds you, and will never let you go.

Receive His peace today — not as something you must manufacture, but as His gift to you in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where are you looking for peace apart from God?
- What does it mean that God's peace is a gift, not an achievement?
- How does Jesus give you peace even in hard circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Prince of Peace, thank You that through the cross I have peace with God. Turn Your face toward me, and fill my troubled heart with Your peace today. Amen.
